sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A PROGRESSIVE/MODERATELY STRONG BELT OF WEST-SOUTHWESTERLY FLOW ALOFT WILL PREVAIL THROUGH THE PERIOD ACROSS THE NORTHERN THIRD TO HALF OF THE CONUS...AS THE SUBTROPICAL HIGH BUILDS A BIT NORTHWARD ACROSS THE SOUTHERN PLAINS/MID-SOUTH. AS HAS BEEN THE CASE FOR THE PAST SEVERAL DAYS...SEVERAL CORRIDORS OF SEVERE STORMS ARE AGAIN LIKELY FROM THE NORTHERN/CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS TO THE MIDWEST AND NORTHEAST STATES.

sections.title: NORTH-CENTRAL PLAINS TO THE UPPER MS VALLEY/MIDWEST
sections.text: ANOTHER ACTIVE DAY APPEARS LIKELY FOR THE REGION. AN EARLY DAY SEVERE STORMS/POSSIBLE MCS...OVER THE DAKOTAS OVERNIGHT...MAY BE SUSTAINED IN SOME FORM AND/OR SHOULD PROVIDE A FOCUS FOR EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD DOWNSTREAM SEVERE TSTM POTENTIAL DURING THE AFTERNOON ACROSS THE UPPER MIDWEST/UPPER MS VALLEY/MIDWEST VICINITY. THE DOWNSTREAM AIRMASS/WARM SECTOR WITHIN THIS CORRIDOR SHOULD AGAIN BECOME MODERATE TO STRONGLY UNSTABLE UNSTABLE...WITH MULTICELLULAR CLUSTERS/SOME SUPERCELLS WITH MAINLY A DAMAGING WIND/SEVERE HAIL POTENTIAL. FARTHER WEST...ARRIVAL OF APPRECIABLE LARGE HEIGHT FALLS AHEAD OF AN EAST-NORTHEAST ADVANCING ROCKIES SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL CONTRIBUTE TO AN UPSWING IN DEEP CONVECTION ACROSS THE NORTH-CENTRAL PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING. THIS IS MOST PROBABLE WITHIN A CORRIDOR FROM THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS INCLUDING EASTERN WY/WESTERN NEB/SOUTHWEST SD...EAST-NORTHEASTWARD ACROSS NEB TO NEAR A SURFACE LOW/TRIPLE POINT ACROSS THE EASTERN DAKOTAS/SOUTHERN MN. STRONG SOUTHWESTERLY FLOW ALOFT/VEERING WIND PROFILES AND AMPLE MOISTURE/ROBUST BUOYANCY WILL SUPPORT A DOMINANT SUPERCELLULAR MODE DURING THE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING HOURS...WITH POTENTIAL FOR VERY LARGE HAIL AND SOME

sections.title: UPPER OH VALLEY/NORTHEAST STATES/DELMARVA
sections.text: SCATTERED CLUSTERS OF THUNDERSTORMS/PERHAPS AN MCS WILL BE ONGOING THIS MORNING ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE UPPER OH RIVER VALLEY/LOWER GREAT LAKES VICINITY. CONVECTIVE REMNANTS/LOW AMPLITUDE SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND A PERSISTENT WEST-SOUTHWESTERLY INSTABILITY FEED/DOWNSTREAM DESTABILIZATION SHOULD CONTRIBUTE TO INCREASING SEVERE TSTM POTENTIAL/COVERAGE THROUGH THE AFTERNOON ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE UPPER OH VALLEY AND NY/PA/DELMARVA VICINITY. STORMS MAY REACH THE ATLANTIC SEABOARD BEFORE SUNSET. DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY CONCERN...WITH SEVERE HAIL POSSIBLE AS WELL. ..GUYER/HURLBUT.. 06/22/2010

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: PERSISTENT SRN PLNS/OZARKS UPR RIDGE WILL BE SUPPRESSED SOMEWHAT S LATER THIS PERIOD AS A PAIR OF POTENT SHORTWAVE IMPULSES NOW OVER THE GRT BASIN SHEAR NE INTO THE CNTRL HI PLNS BY EVE...AND REACH THE UPR MS VLY EARLY WED. AT THE SAME TIME...SYSTEM THAT CROSSED THE GRT LKS LATE YESTERDAY WILL CONTINUE E INTO NEW ENGLAND. AT LWR LVLS...COLD FRONT NOW EVOLVING OVER THE WRN DAKOTAS AND WY SHOULD CONTINUE E/SE THROUGH THE PERIOD...WHILE STNRY FRONT NOW EXTENDING ROUGHLY W-E FROM SRN NEB TO CNTRL IL...DISJOINTED IN SEVERAL PLACES BY CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW...ADVANCES NEWD INTO SE SD/NRN IA. SEVERAL CORRIDORS OF SVR WEATHER ONCE AGAIN APPEAR LIKELY IN A BROAD SWATH FROM THE NRN/CNTRL HI PLNS TO THE MID/UPR MS VLY AND THE NERN STATES. POTENTIALLY THE MOST SIGNIFICANT/WIDESPREAD THREAT...MAINLY IN THE FORM OF HIGH WIND...MAY EVOLVE LATE TONIGHT/EARLY WED OVER PARTS OF NEB/SE SD/IA/SRN MN/SRN WI AND NRN IL.

sections.title: CNTRL HI PLNS TO MID/UPR MS VLY TODAY THROUGH WED MORNING
sections.text: SCTD SMALL CLUSTERS OF STRONG/BRIEFLY SVR ELEVATED STORMS MAY PERSIST THROUGH THIS MORNING ALONG STNRY/WARM FRONT FROM ERN NEB INTO CNTRL IL/IND...SUPPORTED BY LOW LVL WAA/MOISTURE INFLOW. SFC HEATING SHOULD FOSTER THE DEVELOPMENT OF SCTD SFC-BASED BY EARLY AFTN ALONG THE FRONT IN IL/IND...AND PERHAPS A BIT LATER ALONG THE BOUNDARY IN IA AND SE SD. OTHER STORMS LIKELY WILL FORM BY MID-LATE AFTN ALONG DEVELOPING COLD FRONT IN ERN SD/WRN MN...ALONG LEE TROUGH IN ER CO/WRN KS....AND IN POST-FRONTAL UPSLOPE FLOW IN ERN WY/SW SD. GIVEN 40-50 KT DEEP SW TO WLY SHEAR ACROSS THE ENTIRE REGION... AND SBCAPE RANGING FROM AOA 2500 J/KG IN THE HI PLNS TO ABOVE 4000 J/KG IN THE MS VLY...SUSTAINED SUPERCELLS APPEAR LIKELY. IN ADDITION TO POSING A THREAT FOR VERY LARGE HAIL...ESPECIALLY IN THE HI PLNS E INTO CNTRL NEB/SE SD...A THREAT ALSO WILL EXIST FOR TORNADOES. THE LATTER THREAT SHOULD BE GREATEST DURING THE EARLY STAGES OF STORM DEVELOPMENT IN THE HI PLNS...AND INVOF WARM FRONT FROM SE SD ESE INTO IA/SRN MN. AFTN STORMS LIKELY WILL MERGE INTO SEVERAL CLUSTERS THIS EVE...ALONG THE COLD FRONT AND LEE TROUGH IN PARTS OF SD...WRN/NRN NEB AND NW KS...AND ALONG WARM FRONT IN IA/MN/IL. THE POTENTIA

sections.title: UPR OH VLY INTO MID ATLANTIC
sections.text: MOIST...WSWLY LOW LVL MOISTURE INFLOW ON SRN FRINGE OF GRT LKS SHORTWAVE TROUGH...AND SFC HEATING...WILL DESTABILIZE THE MID ATLANTIC STATES AND PARTS OF THE NORTHEAST TODAY. COUPLED WITH ASCENT PROVIDED BY TROUGH...EXPECT SCTD CLUSTERS/BANDS OF STORMS BY MID AFTN ALONG LOW LVL CONFLUENCE AXIS/WEAK FRONT EXTENDING FROM SRN OH/NRN KY INTO WV/MD AND VA. A BAND OF STORMS ALSO MAY FORM ALONG WAA AXIS THROUGH CNTRL NY/PA. DAMAGING WIND SHOULD BE THE PRIMARY CONCERN FROM OH/KY INTO WV. A MORE STRONGLY SHEARED ENVIRONMENT WILL EXIST OVER AND E OF THE MOUNTAINS FROM MD/NRN VA INTO NY/PA...CLOSER TO UPR TROUGH. THERE...A FEW SUPERCELLS MAY WILL BE POSSIBLE...WITH AN ATTENDANT THREAT FOR A TORNADO OR TWO IN ADDITION TO LOCALLY DMGG WIND/MARGINALLY SVR HAIL. ..CORFIDI/GARNER.. 06/22/2010

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: SEVERAL UPPER S/WV TROUGHS/ENHANCED BY OVERNIGHT MCS ACTIVITY ARE TRACKING ACROSS THE TOP OF SRN PLAINS RIDGE AS THE MAIN TROUGH OVER THE WRN U.S. LIFTS NEWD INTO THE HIGH PLAINS BY LATER TONIGHT. INTENSIFYING MID/UPPER WIND MAX WILL ACCOMPANY THE WRN TROUGH ACROSS THE CENTRAL ROCKIES INTO THE PLAINS OVERNIGHT. RESERVOIR OF VERY WARM/MOIST AND UNSTABLE AIR REMAINS AVAILABLE ACROSS MUCH OF THE SRN CONUS E OF ROCKIES FOR FUEL OF THE CONTINUED SERIES OF MCS/S THAT HAVE BEEN HAVE BEEN AFFECTING THE NRN U.S. FROM THE ROCKIES TO THE OH VALLEY FOR SEVERAL DAYS.

sections.title: UPPER OH VALLEY TO THE MID ATLANTIC
sections.text: SHORTWAVE TROUGH...CURRENTLY TRACKING EWD INTO THE LOWER GREAT LAKES/UPPER OH VALLEY PER WATER VAPOR IMAGERY...WILL MOVE EWD INTO NY/PA AND NRN VA/MD THIS AFTERNOON. 12Z UPPER AIR DATA INDICATED 40 KT WLY MIDLEVEL FLOW WITHIN THE BASE OF THIS TROUGH OVER OH. OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS SHOWED EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR ALREADY INCREASING ACROSS CENTRAL PA TO NRN VA AS THE STRONGER FLOW ALOFT SPREADS EWD. IN THE LOW LEVELS...SURFACE FRONT ATTENDANT TO THE SHORTWAVE TROUGH EXTENDED SSWWD FROM SWRN ONTARIO THROUGH CENTRAL OH. THIS BOUNDARY WILL CONTINUE EWD TODAY AND MARK THE WRN EXTENT OF THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT. CLOUDINESS/FILTERED SUNSHINE ACROSS PA...ASSOCIATED WITH CIRRUS AND LEADING BAND OF ONGOING CONVECTION OVER CENTRAL PA TO THE ERN WV PANHANDLE IS LIMITING SURFACE HEATING SOME THIS MORNING. THIS COMBINED WITH WEAK MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES APPEARS TO BE RESULTING IN A SLOWER DESTABILIZATION OF THE AIR MASS THUS FAR. HOWEVER... FURTHER DIABATIC HEATING WITHIN A MOIST AIR MASS IS EXPECTED TO SUPPORT AT LEAST MODERATE INSTABILITY BY THIS AFTERNOON WITH MLCAPE 1000-1500 J/KG EXTENDING FROM OH INTO CENTRAL PA AND SWD TO VA/MD. 12Z WRF-HRRR SUGGESTED THE ONGOING STORMS OVER CENTRAL PA TO ERN WV PAN

sections.title: CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS TO MID/UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: STRONG DAYTIME HEATING SHOULD RELOAD THE INSTABILITY ACROSS MUCH OF THE CENTRAL PLAINS NEWD INTO MID/UPPER MS VALLEY AHEAD OF THE WEAK COLD FRONT FROM THE CENTRAL DAKOTAS SWWD TO THE CENTRAL ROCKIES. GIVEN 40-50 KT DEEP SW TO WLY SHEAR ACROSS THE ENTIRE REGION... AND SBCAPE RANGING FROM AOA 2500 J/KG IN THE HI PLNS TO ABOVE 4000 J/KG IN THE MS VLY...SUSTAINED SUPERCELLS APPEAR LIKELY BY MID/LATE AFTERNOON. IN ADDITION TO POSING A THREAT FOR VERY LARGE HAIL...ESPECIALLY IN THE HI PLNS E INTO CNTRL NEB/SE SD...A THREAT ALSO WILL EXIST FOR TORNADOES. THE LATTER THREAT SHOULD BE GREATEST DURING THE EARLY STAGES OF STORM DEVELOPMENT IN THE HI PLNS...AND INVOF WARM FRONT FROM SE SD ESE INTO IA/SRN MN. AFTN STORMS LIKELY WILL MERGE INTO SEVERAL CLUSTERS THIS EVE...ALONG THE COLD FRONT AND LEE TROUGH IN PARTS OF SD...WRN/NRN NEB AND NW KS...AND ALONG WARM FRONT IN IA/MN/IL. THE POTENTIAL WILL EXIST FOR ONE OF THESE CLUSTERS TO GROW INTO A DERECHO LATE TONIGHT/EARLY WED....MOST LIKELY OVER NERN NEB OR SE SD...AS 50+ KT 500 MB SPEED MAX ASSOCIATED WITH THE GRT BASIN TROUGH OVERSPREADS THE REGION. THIS CONVECTIVE SYSTEM COULD PRODUCE A SWATH OF DMGG WIND E/ESE INTO NRN IL/SRN WI BY 12Z WED. .

sections.title: UPPER OH VALLEY/MID ATLANTIC REGION
sections.text: BOTH THE PRIMARY MID-LEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND MCV HAVE MOVED BEYOND THE LONGITUDE OF THE OH RIVER/LAKE ERIE AT MID-AFTERNOON. LARGE-SCALE SUBSIDENCE IN WAKE OF THESE SYSTEMS WILL INHIBIT SVR THUNDERSTORMS OVER THE CENTRAL GREAT LAKES AND UPPER OH VALLEY THE REMAINDER OF THE PERIOD. MEANWHILE...NARROW INSTABILITY AXIS HAS BEEN TRYING TO DEVELOP NWD OUT OF WV/VA INTO CNTRL PA. THERE WILL REMAIN A CONDITIONAL RISK FOR THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT WITH ATTENDANT DAMAGING WIND/ISOLATED TORNADO RISKS THROUGH EARLY EVENING AS THE PAIR OF UPPER IMPULSES MOVE EWD ACROSS CNTRL/ERN PA...NY AND PARTS OF WV/VA.

STORMS HAVE DEVELOPED ALONG THE CENTRAL/ERN WY RANGES JUST AHEAD OF THE EJECTING MID-LEVEL WAVE. sections.text: UPPER TROUGH OVER WY/SOUTHERN MT EARLY THIS EVENING PER WATER VAPOR IMAGERY WILL CONTINUE TO ADVANCE EAST-NORTHEASTWARD TONIGHT...WITH STRENGTHENING MID/HIGH LEVEL FLOW NOTED PER REGIONAL PROFILERS/WSR-88D DERIVED WINDS ACROSS THE NORTH-CENTRAL PLAINS. SEMI-DISCRETE SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND A TORNADO OR TWO WILL CONTINUE THROUGH MID EVENING ACROSS THE HIGH PLAINS OF WESTERN/CENTRAL NEB AND FAR EASTERN WY TO WESTERN/SOUTHERN SD. HOWEVER...A POTENTIALLY WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WIND THREAT IS LIKELY TO EVOLVE THROUGH THE MID/LATE EVENING HOURS...WITH A COUPLE OF PREFERRED CORRIDORS UNFOLDING. ONE PERHAPS BEING CENTRAL/EASTERN NEB INTO IA ALONG/NORTH OF A PERSISTENT WSW-ENE ORIENTED FRONT...AS WELL AS WEST-CENTRAL/NORTHERN NEB AND SOUTHERN SD AND EVENTUALLY SOUTHWEST MN/NORTHWEST IA...ALONG/SOUTH OF A SOUTHWARD SAGGING WEAK FRONT. sections.title: DELMARVA/MID-ATLANTIC STATES
sections.text: A FEW SEVERE STORMS...CAPABLE OF DAMAGING WINDS/MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL...WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE THIS EVENING MAINLY ACROSS THE DELMARVA VICINITY/ATLANTIC COAST. HOWEVER...THESE STORMS SHOULD GRADUALLY WANE IN INTENSITY OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS AS THEY SPREAD EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS COASTAL AREAS. ..GUYER.. 06/23/2010

mesoscale_discussions.topic: HEAVY RAINFALL VALID 230540Z - 230715Z VERY HEAVY RAIN WITH RAINFALL RATES OF 2 TO 3 INCHES WILL BE LIKELY WITH THE MORE INTENSE STORMS ACROSS NRN IA AND SRN MN OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. LOCALLY HIGHER RAINFALL RATES WILL BE POSSIBLE. A LARGE MCS ONGOING IN NRN IA IS LOCATED ALONG THE NWRN EDGE OF A MOIST AXIS WHERE SFC DEWPOINTS ARE IN THE LOWER TO MID 70S F. PRECIPITABLE WATER VALUES IN NRN IA ARE ESTIMATED BY OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS IN THE 2 TO 2.5 INCH RANGE WITH GPS MEASURING 2.09 INCHES NEAR SIOUX CITY. THIS VERY MOIST AIRMASS COMBINED WITH EXTREME INSTABILITY AND THE SLOW MOVEMENT OF THE MCS SHOULD RESULT IN VERY HEAVY RAINFALL PERSISTENT FOR SEVERAL HOURS ACROSS NRN IA. THIS BAND OF HEAVY RAINFALL WILL SLOWLY SHIFT NNEWD INTO SRN MN EARLY THIS MORNING AS THE NOSE OF A WELL-DEVELOPED LOW-LEVEL JET SHIFTS NEWD INTO THE UPPER MS VALLEY. ..BROYLES.. 06/23/2010 ATTN
